public_evidence.algorithm: DFlash2 block-diffusion speculative drafter with a candidate path selector and two-tap dynamic depthwise convolutions

failure_reasons: mixed-prompt speedup 1.287x is below the frozen 1.40x diagnostic-retention floor
one deterministic greedy prompt diverged from target-only
29.91 GiB peak RSS exceeds the frozen 28.5 GiB safety gate

mismatch_diagnostic.prompt: Explain in four sentences why CPU language-model decode is memory-bandwidth bound.

confirmed: DFlash2 is implemented for the exact Qwen3.8-27B target and runs on the AMD CPU backend.
Its gain is highly prompt-dependent because acceptance ranged from a full seven-token block to roughly two committed tokens per target call.
llama.cpp CPU repacking consumed about 9 GiB without improving target-only or high-acceptance DFlash2 throughput on this node.
Disabling repacking restored exact greedy parity in this three-prompt smoke and reduced peak RSS by 8.94 GiB.
Neither tested configuration beats the qualified 3.611857 tok/s v23 MTP3 result on the mixed prompt set.
interpretation.inference: The high-leverage kernel target is an exact, memory-lean Q4_K verification path for block widths up to eight. It must preserve batch-1 numerical behavior while retaining the high-acceptance speed seen with DFlash2. Admission or fallback must avoid full DFlash blocks when selector confidence predicts low acceptance.
not_established: that the repack path alone caused the greedy mismatch
capability preservation beyond exact greedy smoke parity
